note: Platte River access in Andrew County woods, on the site of an 1800s flour mill. The camping spot is beside a small gravel lot at the end of a short lane off County Road 216 (this pin); a dirt track runs on toward the river. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: area page 'Camping: Individual Campsites' and 'Camping is permitted in designated areas and is limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period'; GIS 'Primitive Camping Area' point 115 ~20 m from gravel lot 73. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights written manual. PIN: GIS point is in trees beside the lot -> move to the lot 39.99925,-94.69320 (20 m). Not waterfront kept. Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: area page 'Things to Do When You Visit': 'Camping: Individual Campsites'; regulation 140: 'Camping is permitted in designated areas and is limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period. Groups of 10 or more people must obtain a special-use permit.' Brochure (01/2022) repeats it and 'No open fires. Pitted fires only in designated areas.' No area map is posted. MDC's GIS has one camping point (115, Type 'Primitive Camping Area') ~20 m SSE of the only lot (73): a mapped designated spot beside a gravel lot, not a boat-ramp lot, so it stays. Imagery (leaf-off): a gravel turnaround ~30 x 20 m at the west end of a ~120 m gravel lane off County Road 216, in woods, with a dirt track leading south past the camp point toward the river. A 23-ft rig fits the turnaround. No ford/4WD/rig wording.
PIN: stored 39.99909,-94.69308 = GIS camp point 115, which is under trees beside the dirt track. Move to the lot, 39.99925,-94.69320 (GIS lot 73, 20 m).
WATERFRONT (not waterfront, kept): the Platte River (~35-45 m wide) is ~100-120 m SW of the lot and camp point through woods and a sandy bank.
PHONE: area page and brochure '(816) 271-3100' (the St. Joseph office) match.
